chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from his father, who attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) that he said:

The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said: 'Whoever asks you by Allah, give to him; and whoever does a good turn to you, recompense him. If you do not find anything to recompense him with, then pray to Allah for him until you feel sure that you have recompensed him.'
ai.seo_question: What should I do if I cannot repay someone who did me a favor?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, emphasizes the spiritual weight of social reciprocity (*mu'asharah*) by linking material gratitude to divine supplication. It instructs believers to fulfill requests made in Allah's name and, when material recompense is insufficient, to engage in earnest prayer for the benefactor until they feel their debt is fully settled. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining social bonds through both tangible action and spiritual intercession.
